guide.title: Montville, Connecticut: Mohegan Ground on the Oxoboxo
guide.intro: Montville separated from New London and incorporated as its own town in 1786; its name signifies "mountain village," and it now comprises four principal villages — Chesterfield, Mohegan, Oakdale, and Uncasville. Rocky, forested terrain made farming difficult, so the town turned to waterpower instead: early enterprises smelted bog ore into iron, and by the late 1800s manufacturers lined the Oxoboxo River. Montville's deeper history centers on the Mohegan people: in the seventeenth century, sachem Uncas established a fortified village at Fort Shantok above the Thames River, the tribe's principal settlement from 1636 to 1682, which withstood a Narragansett siege there in 1645. Mohegan medicine woman and anthropologist Gladys Tantaquidgeon co-founded the Tantaquidgeon Museum in 1931 with her father and brother; her research later helped the Mohegan Tribe win federal recognition in 1994. The tribe's 700-acre reservation, a sovereign nation within Montville's borders, is now home to the Mohegan Sun casino resort.

sections.heading: Mohegan ground on the Oxoboxo
sections.body: Montville separated from New London and incorporated as its own town in 1786; its name signifies "mountain village," and it now comprises four principal villages — Chesterfield, Mohegan, Oakdale, and Uncasville. Rocky, forested terrain made farming difficult, so the town turned to waterpower instead: early enterprises smelted bog ore into iron, and by the late 1800s manufacturers lined the Oxoboxo River. Montville's deeper history centers on the Mohegan people: in the seventeenth century, sachem Uncas established a fortified village at Fort Shantok above the Thames River, the tribe's principal settlement from 1636 to 1682, which withstood a Narragansett siege there in 1645. Mohegan medicine woman and anthropologist Gladys Tantaquidgeon co-founded the Tantaquidgeon Museum in 1931 with her father and brother; her research later helped the Mohegan Tribe win federal recognition in 1994.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: Montville is a drive-to destination on the west bank of the Thames River, reached via I-395 and CT Route 32 (the Norwich-New London Turnpike). There is no train station in town — the nearest Amtrak service is in New London, about 10 minutes south on Route 32.

sections.heading: Mohegan Sun and the villages beyond
sections.body: The tribe's 700-acre reservation, a sovereign nation within Montville's borders, is home to the Mohegan Sun casino resort, opened in 1996 with a 10,000-seat arena and more than 35 restaurants, bars, and cafes. The Tantaquidgeon Museum, the oldest Native American-owned and operated museum in the United States, traces Mohegan heritage from prehistoric times to the present, while Fort Shantok, a National Historic Landmark since 1993, marks the tribe's seventeenth-century settlement above the Thames. Uncasville's Norwich-New London Turnpike carries a strip of longtime local restaurants outside the reservation.

faq.question: How do I get to Montville?
faq.answer: Montville is reached via I-395 and CT Route 32 (the Norwich-New London Turnpike). There is no train station in town; the nearest Amtrak service is in New London, about 10 minutes south on Route 32.

faq.question: What is Mohegan Sun?
faq.answer: A casino resort on the sovereign Mohegan reservation within Montville, opened in 1996, with a 10,000-seat arena, more than 35 restaurants, bars, and cafes, an 18-hole golf course, a spa, and 30-plus shops.

faq.question: What is the Tantaquidgeon Museum?
faq.answer: The oldest Native American-owned and operated museum in the United States, established in 1931 by Gladys Tantaquidgeon with her brother Harold and father John; its collections trace Mohegan heritage from prehistoric times to the present. Visits are by appointment — call (860) 862-0875 ahead.

faq.question: What is Fort Shantok?
faq.answer: The site of the principal Mohegan settlement from 1636 to 1682, associated with sachem Uncas, designated the Fort Shantok Archaeological District, a National Historic Landmark, in 1993, and returned to Mohegan control in 1995.

faq.question: Where can I stay in Montville?
faq.answer: Mohegan Sun's Sky Tower and Earth Tower, with about 1,600 rooms and suites combined, are the town's verified lodging option; no independent historic inn or B&B in Montville could be verified as currently operating.

places.name: Tantaquidgeon Museum
places.summary: The oldest Native American-owned and operated museum in the United States, established in 1931 by Gladys Tantaquidgeon with her brother Harold and father John; collections trace Mohegan heritage from prehistoric times to the present, with a reconstructed traditional dwelling outdoors. Visits are by appointment — call (860) 862-0875 ahead.

places.name: Fort Shantok (Shantok, Village of Uncas)
places.summary: Site of the principal Mohegan settlement 1636-1682 and sacred ground associated with sachem Uncas; designated the Fort Shantok Archaeological District, a National Historic Landmark, in 1993, and returned from state park ownership to Mohegan control in 1995. The Mohegan Tribe operates the grounds as a local park within the reservation.

places.name: Michael Jordan's Steak House

places.name: The Dinosaur Place at Nature's Art Village
places.summary: Sixty acres of family attraction built around a mile and a half of nature trails lined with more than a hundred life-sized dinosaur sculptures, plus a splash pad, the A-MAZE-asaurus maze, Monty's Playground, a gem-mining and gold-panning Discovery Depot, and an adjoining mini-golf course. Admission is charged; check current pricing before you go.
